take_homes: Don't guess which quality check works. Run several on my own material and keep the one the scores back up.
The judge file says what it catches and what it can't, so a teammate can pick it up and trust it only as far as it goes.
Make the agent re-read the file after it edits it. Its summary describes what it meant to do, not what's there.

monday.move: Run the judge on the pilot-cohort brief with fresh data before it goes to the pricing working group, and flag anything ungrounded.
monday.who: Me, then one person from my team of fourteen to check the flags.
monday.when: Monday morning, before the working group send-out.
monday.stop_condition: If the judge flags more than a handful of ungrounded claims, I hold the brief and fix the sources first.
monday.blocker: There's no shared place for the judge file and context files, so each person would have their own copy.

misconception.why: The scoreboard showed the quality gain comes from a measured check, not from phrasing. Prompts still matter a bit, but a tested judge file did more than a clever prompt would have.

one_line: Good hands-on module: you test four checks on your own briefing and keep the winner as a file. The prework and the legal-case examples are skippable.
